entries.title: Separator witness for percolation gluing
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF; independent audit pending. Let G be a finite undirected graph with vertices o,b, a nonempty relay set A, a vertex v, and a_star in A. If every o-to-A path and every a_star-to-b path contains v, then in every edge configuration {o connects to A,a_star connects to b} is contained in {o connects to b,o connects to A}. For independent Bernoulli edge states with arbitrary edge probabilities in [0,1], P(o connects to b)>=P(o connects to A)min_{a in A}P(a connects to b). Connection means an open path in G.
entries.proof_text: On the intersected event, a chosen open o-to-A path supplies an open o-to-v segment, and an open a_star-to-b path supplies an open v-to-b segment. Concatenate to connect o to b. Harris positive association bounds the intersection probability below by the product of the two increasing-event probabilities.
assumptions: The two separator hypotheses hold for deterministic G,v,a_star
Independent Bernoulli edge states with arbitrary probabilities in [0,1] only for the probabilistic product conclusion

entries.title: Gluing with arbitrary many relays in a finite forest
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF; independent audit pending. Let G be any finite undirected forest, o,b any vertices, and A any nonempty vertex set. For independent Bernoulli edge states with arbitrary edge probabilities in [0,1], P(o connects to b)>=P(o connects to A)min_{a in A}P(a connects to b). There is also a deterministic a_star in A such that {o connects to A,a_star connects to b} is contained in {o connects to b,o connects to A} in every configuration. Consequently P(o connects to b,o connects to A)>=min_{a in A}P(o connects to A,a connects to b) holds for any edge-state law. The product inequality's coefficient 1 is sharp. Connection means an open path; overlap of terminals and relays, disconnected forests, and o=b are allowed.
entries.proof_text: If A has a vertex outside b's graph component, the minimum connection probability is zero; if o and b are in different graph components then either this happens or P(o connects to A)=0. Otherwise all relevant vertices lie in one tree. Project each relay to the unique o-b path and choose the projection nearest o, denoted v, and a relay a_star attaining it. Every o-to-A path contains v and every a_star-to-b path contains v. Apply L1. A three-vertex path o-a-b with A={a} attains equality for any positive edge probabilities, proving sharpness.

entries.title: Sharp near-one gluing modulus in finite forests
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF; independent audit pending. For each epsilon in (0,1), delta_star=1-sqrt(1-epsilon) is the largest delta in (0,1] such that the following implication holds for every finite forest G, independent Bernoulli edge probabilities in [0,1], vertices o,b and nonempty relay set A: if P(o connects to A)>1-delta and P(a connects to b)>1-delta for all a in A, then P(o connects to b)>1-epsilon. A two-edge path rules out every larger delta, so delta_star is also a necessary upper bound on any proposed all-finite-graph modulus. Its sufficiency for arbitrary cyclic graphs is not asserted.
entries.proof_text: L2 gives terminal probability > (1-delta_star)^2=1-epsilon. For any larger delta choose a two-edge path o-a-b with both probabilities x strictly between max(0,1-delta) and sqrt(1-epsilon); the premises hold but x^2<1-epsilon.
assumptions: Independent Bernoulli bond states with arbitrary edge probabilities in [0,1]
Strict premises and conclusion as in Kozma-Nitzan Conjecture 3

entries.title: Relay selection can destroy terminal connectivity
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF; independent audit pending. In independent bond percolation on the path o--a2--a1--b, give successive edges probabilities r,s,t in (0,1) and order A=(a1,a2). Let I be the first member of A connected to o, undefined when o misses A. Then P(I=a2)=r(1-s)>0 but P(a2 connects to b | I=a2)=0<P(a2 connects to b)=st. Moreover P(o connects to b)=rst while sum_{a in A}P(I=a)P(a connects to b)=rst(2-s)>rst. For r=s=t=1/2 these are 1/8 and 3/16. This refutes unconditional substitution or the averaged bridge for arbitrary relay order, without refuting product gluing or claims requiring a nondecreasing terminal-marginal order.
entries.proof_text: P(I=a1)=rs, P(I=a2)=r(1-s), and P(a1 connects to b)=t, P(a2 connects to b)=st. Conditioning on I=a2 forces the middle edge closed, so its conditional terminal probability is 0. P(o connects to b)=rst, but the averaged unconditional relay sum is rst(2-s), larger by rst(1-s)>0. At r=s=t=1/2 the true probability is 1/8 and the sum 3/16.

entries.title: A square prevents a fixed pointwise relay witness
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF; independent audit pending. Let G have vertices o,a1,a2,v,b, exactly the edges o-a1,a1-v,o-a2,a2-v,v-b, and A={a1,a2}. No fixed a_star in A satisfies {o connects to A,a_star connects to b} subset {o connects to b} for every edge configuration. With each independent edge probability 1/2, P(o connects to b)=7/32, P(o connects to A)=3/4, and min_{a in A}P(a connects to b)=9/32, so product gluing still holds with margin 1/128. Thus only a universal deterministic-witness bridge is refuted, not stochastic gluing.
entries.proof_text: For a_star=a1 open exactly o-a2,a1-v,v-b; for a_star=a2 interchange the relay names. Each selection violates the claimed event inclusion. At half weights product gluing remains valid: 7/32-(3/4)(9/32)=1/128.
assumptions: All independent edge probabilities strictly between 0 and 1 to obtain positive-probability failures

entries.title: Refuted arbitrary-order selected-relay bridge
entries.statement: REFUTED AUXILIARY PROPOSITION, not a theorem: after selecting the first member I of an arbitrarily ordered relay set A reached from o in independent bond percolation, replace P(a connects to b | I=a) by a lower bound P(a connects to b), or assert P(o connects to b)>=sum_a P(I=a)P(a connects to b). This proposition is false on o--a2--a1--b with relay order (a1,a2). A specified nondecreasing marginal order is a separate proposition. The original product and near-one gluing assertions are not refuted.

entries.title: Refuted universal fixed-relay witness bridge
entries.statement: REFUTED AUXILIARY PROPOSITION, not a theorem: for every finite graph and nonempty relay set A there is a deterministic a_star in A such that {o connects to A,a_star connects to b} is contained in {o connects to b}. A square o--a1--v--a2--o with a pendant edge v--b and A={a1,a2} is a counterexample. The inclusion does hold for forests; failure of this deterministic bridge does not refute probabilistic gluing.

relations.rationale: L2: 'every finite forest' admits the fixed separator demanded by L1: 'v lies on every o-to-A path and every a_star-to-b path'. Tree projection supplies both hypotheses; no arbitrary cyclic extension is asserted.
L3's 'delta_star=1-sqrt(1-epsilon)' follows by applying L2's 'product gluing inequality' to the two strict near-one premises; two-edge paths establish necessity.
B1: 'conditional terminal probability is 0' and 'rst(2-s)' exceeds 'rst', directly refuting the concept's replacement of selected conditional marginals and its arbitrary-order averaged inequality.
B2: 'For a_star=a1 open exactly o-a2,a1-v,v-b; for a_star=a2 interchange the relay names' excludes every candidate required by the concept's universal pointwise witness assertion.
L2's forest witness meets its boundary at B2's square; B2 explicitly leaves the probability product bound intact (margin 1/128 at half weights).
